title: Jordan's 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record $14m
title_zh: 乔丹“最后一舞”球衣拍出1400万美元天价

image.credit: Photo by Keith Christian Armada on Unsplash
image.author: Keith Christian Armada

lead: A Michael Jordan jersey from his final season with the Chicago Bulls has sold for $14m, setting a new record for basketball memorabilia.
lead_zh: 迈克尔·乔丹在芝加哥公牛队最后一个赛季穿过的一件球衣以1400万美元售出，创下篮球纪念品的新纪录。

paragraphs: Jordan wore the jersey during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals, and he also signed it. He scored 37 points that night, which was the highest score in the game.
He then ended his last season with the Bulls by winning the series 4-2. It was his sixth and final NBA Championship, and he was named Finals MVP all six times.
The only sports memorabilia that has sold for more is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth in the 1932 World Series, which sold for $24.1m in 2024.
The previous record for a basketball item was a 2007-08 card featuring Jordan and Kobe Bryant, which sold for $12.9m last year. Just two weeks ago, another Jordan jersey sold for $12.3m.
Miami real estate investor Ron Firman bought the jersey in a private sale through Hunt Auctions. David Hunt, the auction house president, said Jordan items have become an elite asset class.

随后他带领公牛队以4比2赢下系列赛，结束了在公牛队的最后一个赛季。这是他第六个也是最后一个NBA总冠军，而且六次都当选总决赛最有价值球员。
唯一比它更贵的体育纪念品，是棒球传奇贝比·鲁斯在1932年世界大赛中穿过的球衣，那件在2024年拍出了2410万美元。
此前篮球物品的最高纪录是一张2007-08赛季的乔丹和科比双人卡，去年以1290万美元售出。就在两周前，另一件乔丹球衣也拍出了1230万美元。
迈阿密房地产投资人罗恩·菲尔曼通过亨特拍卖行以私下交易方式买下了这件球衣。拍卖行总裁大卫·亨特表示，乔丹的物品已经成了一种顶级资产。

title_original: Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
summary_original: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
body_original:
Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
By
Ben Collins
BBC Sport journalist
Published
5 hours ago
A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season has sold for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
Jordan wore the Chicago Bulls jersey during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals and has autographed it too.
He scored a game-high 37 points that evening before ending his last season with the Bulls with a 4-2 series win for his sixth and final NBA Championship. He was named the Finals' Most Valuable Player in all six.
The only item of sports memorabilia that has cost more is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he "called the shot" during the 1932 World Series, which was sold for $24.1m (£18.2m) in 2024.
The previous high for a basketball item was a card featuring Jordan and Kobe Bryant from 2007-08 which
sold for $12.9m (£9.8m) last year.
The previous record for a piece of game-worn Jordan memorabilia was set just two weeks ago when his jersey from game three of the 1998 Finals, which is not autographed,
sold via auction for $12.3m (£9.3m).
The latest purchase was made by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale through Hunt Auctions.
David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement: "While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art."
